title: thymus chamaedrys var. pulegioides
intro: Thymus chamaedrys var. pulegioides, commonly known as wild marjoram or pulegium, is a subspecies of the thyme plant belonging to the Lamiaceae family. This plant has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of wild marjoram include its ability to soothe digestive issues, relieve respiratory problems, and act as a natural antiseptic. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include carvacrol, thymol, and rosmarinic acid, which are known for their ability to fight infections and reduce inflammation.
